title.notes: The artist/act name for each of the 4 events currently shown (the whole visible agenda at this fresh fetch time, unchanged from casa-independente-lisbon-01's sample) is directly stated in a plain <h1> inside a text-editor widget immediately following each date block and a short event-type heading — no combination with surrounding context is needed, so DIRECT_SOURCE, not DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT. All 4 sampled events still carry the event-type label 'DJ Set'. Value is recorded as the array of all 4 sampled titles rather than a single scalar, honestly reflecting that this field_assessment describes a bounded multi-event sample, not one single event.

start_date.notes: Each event block states its own day + 3-letter Portuguese month abbreviation (e.g. '21 AGO') but no event block states its own year. The year is stated exactly once, in the single page-level 'Agosto 2026' heading, which this fresh fetch again shows as the ONLY month/year heading on the page. Combining the two per event (day/month from the card, year from the page heading) is a mechanical, source-derived combination, not a guess based on today's date. All 4 derived dates were cross-checked against the source's own weekday label via pure calendar math (4/4 matched, evidence/offline-proof-output.txt Step 2) — the same corroboration casa-independente-lisbon-01 performed, reproduced here against a freshly fetched, independently retained fixture. This value array is identical to casa-independente-lisbon-01's own 4 derived dates, which is itself the central, mechanically-verified finding of this investigation (see decision.reasons and evidence/offline-proof-output.txt Step 4): two calendar days apart, nothing changed. Timing remains floating-local: no explicit timezone/UTC offset is stated anywhere in the retained HTML.

derivation.rule: The single page-level month/year heading (format '<MonthName> <Year>') governs every event row beneath it until a next such heading would appear (none does in this retained fetch — only one heading exists). Combine the heading's <MonthName> <Year> with each row's own '<DD> <MonthAbbrev>' day/month line to yield '<Year>-<MM>-<DD>' per row. Applied identically to all 4 sampled rows.

time.notes: Each event block states an hour-only time (e.g. '23H' = 23:00) on the same date heading as the day/month. No minutes and no timezone/offset are stated anywhere in the freshly retained HTML for any of the 4 sampled events. Recorded as PARTIAL rather than PROVEN under v1.2's stricter non-null-value-when-PROVEN rule: hour-only precision, with no minutes and no timezone, is not confidently promotable to a precise claimed value the way a full HH:MM (even floating-local) would be. Not padded with an invented ':00' presented as more precise than it is.

end.notes: No end time or end date is stated anywhere in the freshly retained HTML for any of the 4 sampled events — only a single start hour per event. The source genuinely does not expose this fact.

venue_location.notes: Casa Independente is a single-venue site — the /agenda/ page itself never repeats an address per event. The freshly retained /contactos/ page states the venue's own street address, and the freshly retained /sobre/ page independently re-corroborates the same 'Largo do Intendente' location in its own founding-history prose. The freshly retained /agenda/ page itself never names or references any other venue, location, room name, or address anywhere in its markup (checked mechanically in evidence/offline-proof-output.txt Step 7 — no alternate street-type prefix, e.g. 'Rua'/'Avenida'/'Praça', appears anywhere on the page). Since this is a closed, single-venue site with no other candidate location ever mentioned across any of the retained pages, the one stated address applies uniformly to all 4 sampled events. This mirrors, but freshly re-establishes, casa-independente-lisbon-01's own conclusion.

derivation.rule: If a source's complete retained set of pages (agenda + homepage + contacts + about) states exactly one venue name/address and no other venue, room, or location is ever referenced anywhere across that retained set, then every event listed on that source's own agenda page is hosted at that one venue.
inputs: the freshly retained agenda page never names any other venue/location anywhere in its markup

source_record_id.notes: Re-confirmed freshly: no id, slug, data-attribute, or any other machine identifier exists anywhere in the freshly retained /agenda/ HTML for any individual event — still only Elementor's own internal element ids (e.g. 'data-id="32bfc0d4"'), which are editor-authoring artifacts, not stable per-event identifiers (evidence/offline-proof-output.txt Step 5 lists 51 such data-id attributes on this fresh fetch, all Elementor internals). Per the stable-identifier rule, this stays honestly NOT_PRESENT. ALTERNATIVE IDENTITY STRATEGY (documented per policy, not proven, unchanged from casa-independente-lisbon-01): a future collector could synthesize a composite key from (venue_reference + derived ISO date + normalised artist-name slug), e.g. 'casa-independente-2026-08-21-didi'. This remains workable for the observed one-act-per-date-slot pattern but has still never been empirically tested against two acts sharing one date/time slot — this fresh fetch's 4-event sample, like the original's, never exhibited that case.

event_url.notes: Re-confirmed freshly: no individual event detail page or per-event URL exists anywhere on this site within this fresh fetch — every event's only information lives directly on the shared /agenda/ page. evidence/offline-proof-output.txt Step 5 enumerates all 18 distinct href values on the fresh agenda page and confirms none matches a per-event detail-link pattern. A collector could only ever cite the single shared https://casaindependente.com/agenda/ URL for every event, which is not a unique per-event URL and stays honestly NOT_PRESENT.

price.notes: No price, admission fee, or free-entry label is stated anywhere in the freshly retained HTML for any of the 4 sampled events. The source genuinely does not expose this fact.

blockers.description: The source still exposes no per-event id and no per-event URL at all, re-confirmed against this fresh 2026-08-27 fetch. A collector has no source-documented stable identity to anchor an Observation to and must rely entirely on a synthesized composite key (venue + derived date + artist-name slug) and the single shared agenda-page URL for every event. Still untested against same-date/same-slot double-bookings, artist-name spelling drift between visits, or the source silently re-typing/removing a past event without a trace.

The month-boundary question this investigation was specifically created to resolve remains UNRESOLVED. Fetched fresh on 2026-08-27 — 2 calendar days after casa-independente-lisbon-01's 2026-08-25 fetch, and inside the 'late August 2026' window that investigation flagged for re-observation — the page's event-relevant content (heading text + all 4 event blocks) is mechanically confirmed BYTE-IDENTICAL to the original fixture (evidence/offline-proof-output.txt Step 4). The source has simply not yet transitioned to publishing September content: today (2026-08-27) has not yet crossed into September, so there is still no real month boundary to observe on this source's own agenda page. A collector built against the single-heading-governs-all-cards assumption remains unvalidated against a genuine multi-month page state — this fetch could not manufacture that state; it could only confirm that August's single-heading page has not (yet) changed shape.

The source's own weekday-label text remains inconsistently formatted even within this re-fetched 4-event sample ('SEXTA FEIRA' vs 'SEXTA' for the same weekday), re-confirming the page is hand-typed per event, not template-generated. Does not currently break date parsing (only the numeric 'DD MES' line is load-bearing).
No admission price/ticket information and no event end-time are exposed for any sampled event in this fresh fetch either; both fields remain honestly NOT_PRESENT rather than fabricated.

THE CENTRAL, DELIBERATELY-SOUGHT FINDING OF THIS INVESTIGATION: the month-boundary question casa-independente-lisbon-01 explicitly deferred on is STILL NOT RESOLVED, but now for a mechanically-verified, honest reason rather than an open question. A fresh fetch 2 calendar days later, plus a cache-busted duplicate fetch confirming no stale-cache artifact, both show the page's event-relevant content is byte-identical to the original 2026-08-25 fixture (evidence/offline-proof-output.txt Step 4) — still exactly one 'Agosto 2026' heading, still the same 4 events. This is because 2026-08-27 has not yet crossed into September; the source has simply not had a real month boundary to react to yet. This investigation therefore could not observe how a second heading would appear, whether past events get removed, or whether the whole page gets replaced — the same MAJOR blocker as before, now re-confirmed with fresh, independently-retained, cache-verified evidence rather than carried over as an assumption.

The source_record_id/event_url gap is unchanged and freshly re-confirmed: still no per-event id or URL exists anywhere on the page. The same alternative composite-key identity strategy (venue + derived ISO date + normalised artist-name slug) remains documented in field_assessment.source_record_id.notes, satisfying the READY_FOR_ACTIVATION gate's 'PROVEN OR alternative strategy documented' condition structurally — but this investigation still deliberately does not recommend READY_FOR_ACTIVATION given the unresolved MAJOR month-boundary blocker above.

This decision therefore stays at READY_FOR_OFFLINE_PROOF, matching casa-independente-lisbon-01's own conclusion — but this is now itself a mechanically-verified, evidenced re-confirmation (not a default/unchanged carry-over) that the same blocker genuinely still applies. The honest recommendation is a THIRD future observation of https://casaindependente.com/agenda/ made after the calendar has genuinely crossed into September 2026 and enough time has passed for the venue to plausibly have updated the page (the page is clearly hand-maintained and not necessarily updated on the first of the month) — that future investigation should be a new investigation_id with supersedes pointing back at this one.
This decision is a research conclusion only — it does not edit sources/*.json or any registry.
